# Relay stage 3: Diagnose
Task: 05-shfmt-shell-format-guard
Working directory: /Users/admin/Dev/visual-relay/
Protected paths (queue bookkeeping — never part of this task's diff): llm-tasks/, .relay/, .relay-scratch/, .swival/

## Task input
# Enforce shfmt formatting through the shell guard, with a bootstrap carve-out

The shell-size guard counts logic lines, so its 20-line ceiling is satisfied
by layout, not size: `visual-relay` packs whole functions into ~300-470-char
`;`-chained one-liners and passes at 16 logic lines. Formatted honestly it is
68. Measured with shfmt 3.13.1 (nixpkgs) over every tracked shell script:
`visual-relay` 16→68, `.githooks/command-guard` 18→21, `.githooks/commit-msg`
20→20, `.githooks/pre-commit` 19→19, `me.sh` 4, `test.sh` 3,
`tools/dotnet-test-files.sh` 12→14. The output is idempotent and preserves
every comment. The fix: make machine formatting mandatory — a crammed script
can no longer hide lines — raise the general ceiling from 20 to 24 so honestly
formatted wrappers keep headroom (post-format `command-guard` is 21; a 20
ceiling survives only via hand-tuning, which is the disease this task cures),
and give the one genuinely irreducible script (the pre-dotnet bootstrap) a
100-line ceiling. No line-length enforcement; formatting is the anti-gaming
mechanism.

## Prescribed approach

shfmt becomes a devshell tool (nix only, never a global install). The shell
guard enforces BOTH the size limits and the formatting: `./visual-relay format`
applies `shfmt --write`; the guard surfaces (`guards` shell-size subcommand and
the `check` gate) verify with `shfmt --diff` and fail on drift. The
guard-as-test (`ShellScriptSizeGuardTests`) stays pure C# with no shfmt
dependency — exactly as C# formatting is enforced by `check`'s
`dotnet format --verify-no-changes`, not by a test. The general ceiling
becomes 24; `visual-relay` (exact root-relative path) gets a fixed
100-logic-line ceiling.

### Steps

1. flake.nix: add `shfmt` to the devshell packages list.
2. Limits, in tools/VisualRelay.Guards: raise `ShellSizeGuard.DefaultLimit`
   from 20 to 24; add `BootstrapLimit = 100` and `BootstrapPath =
   "visual-relay"` constants; `FindViolations` applies `BootstrapLimit` when a
   file's relative path equals `BootstrapPath` (ordinal), the passed limit
   otherwise, so `Violation.Limit` reports the ceiling that actually applied.
   `VISUAL_RELAY_SHELL_LINE_LIMIT` and the runner's `--max` keep overriding
   only the general limit; the bootstrap ceiling is a fixed constant with no
   knob. Update `ShellSizeGuardRunner`'s remediation line — "there is no
   allowlist" is no longer true; say the bootstrap is the single structural
   carve-out and all other logic moves to C#.
3. Shared enumeration: extract a `TrackedShellScripts` helper in
   VisualRelay.Guards (git `ls-files` through `IGitInvoker`, filter through
   `ShellScriptClassifier`, skip missing/unreadable files) and consume it from
   `ShellSizeGuardRunner`, the Cli `GuardRunner.ShellSizeAsync` gate, and the
   new format code. Three copies of that enumeration loop must not exist
   afterward.
4. Formatting check: add `ShellFormatGuard` to VisualRelay.Guards running
   `shfmt --diff -- <files>` via `ProcessCapture.RunAsync`, with NO style or
   dialect flags — a bare invocation keeps `.editorconfig` in charge (today no
   section matches shell scripts, so canonical output is shfmt defaults:
   tabs). Exit 0 → clean. Exit 1 → print the diff and
   "run ./visual-relay format". Missing binary → "shfmt not found; run through
   ./visual-relay so the nix devshell provides it" and fail — an enforcing
   guard treats a missing tool as a failure, not a pass.
5. Wire it: the `shell-size` guards subcommand and `GuardRunner.ShellSizeAsync`
   run the size check then the format check, reporting both kinds of violation
   before failing. Update the Program.cs dispatch comment, the `GuardRunner`
   and `CheckCommand` doc comments. `build` stays untouched (it runs only the
   source-enumeration guard today).
6. Apply path: after `dotnet format` succeeds, `FormatCommand` runs
   `shfmt --write -- <files>` over the same enumeration (the command goes
   async). `format` stays the single apply entry point.
7. Reformat the tree with `./visual-relay format` and commit shfmt's output
   verbatim — zero hand edits to script code. The only script text edited by
   hand is the bootstrap's own header comment, whose stated ceiling ("keep
   this file ≤20 logic lines") becomes the new 100.
8. Tests, in tests/VisualRelay.Tests: retarget the constant-pin test
   (`DefaultLimit_IsThe20LineCeiling` → asserts 24, rename to match) and pin
   `BootstrapLimit` at 100 beside it; move the at-limit synthetic in
   `OverLimitScript_IsAViolation_AtLimitScript_IsNot` from 20 to 24 (25 stays
   the over sample); extend the `FindViolations` unit tests — a synthetic
   `visual-relay` at 100 logic lines passes, at 101 violates with
   `Limit: 100`, and a nested `sub/visual-relay` still gets the general 24.
   Rewrite the `ShellScriptSizeGuardTests` doc comment: drop "no
   allowlist"/"never excused", state the bootstrap carve-out and that
   formatting is enforced by the `check` gate, not this test. Refresh the
   stale "20-line POSIX limit" comment in `WindowsLauncherSizeGuardTests`.
9. AGENTS.md: extend the Build & checks section — shell scripts are
   shfmt-formatted (apply with `./visual-relay format`, verified by `check`),
   scripts stay ≤ 24 logic lines with the bootstrap's 100-line carve-out.

### Guardrails

- No shfmt in any test. Bare `dotnet test` on the tests project outside the
  devshell must stay green; the guard-as-test remains a pure line counter.
- No global shfmt: not brew, not a checked-in binary, no PATH fallback logic
  beyond the devshell.
- No style flags and no `.editorconfig` shell section. Default shfmt output
  (tabs) is canonical, and passing printer flags would disable shfmt's native
  EditorConfig support.
- No line-length enforcement. Explicitly deferred; do not add a max-width
  check anywhere.
- Never hand-edit script code to satisfy the meter — no inlining, no
  `;`-joining, no restructuring. A wrapper that outgrows 24 moves its logic
  to C#. Comment edits are fine; layout belongs to shfmt.
- Formatting `visual-relay` while it runs is safe — the `main()` wrapper makes
  bash parse everything before any subcommand executes. Do not "fix" that.
- release.yml only publishes; it never runs `check` or tests, so CI needs no
  shfmt. Verify, do not wire it.

## Done when

Inside the devshell: `./visual-relay check` is green end-to-end; re-running
`./visual-relay format` is a no-op; hand-mangling the formatting of any one
script makes `./visual-relay guards` and `check` fail with the diff and the
remediation hint. Outside the devshell: bare `dotnet test` on the tests
project is green. All seven tracked scripts are committed shfmt-formatted,
`visual-relay` is within 100 logic lines, and every other script is within 24
with no hand-modified script code.

## Commit-message evidence

Measure at implementation time and put in the commit body (≤ 3 hyphen bullets,
≤ 20 words each, no file names or paths): per-script logic-line counts before
vs after formatting against their ceilings, and the format-then-verify no-op
proof.

Now I have a thorough understanding of the codebase. Here is my diagnosis:

---

## Diagnosis

### 1. Seven tracked shell scripts and their current state

| Script | Current logic lines | Post-shfmt logic lines | Ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `visual-relay` | 16 | ~68 | 100 (bootstrap) |
| `.githooks/command-guard` | 18 | ~21 | 24 |
| `.githooks/commit-msg` | 20 | 20 | 24 |
| `.githooks/pre-commit` | 19 | 19 | 24 |
| `me.sh` | 4 | 4 | 24 |
| `test.sh` | 3 | 3 | 24 |
| `tools/dotnet-test-files.sh` | 12 | ~14 | 24 |

The `visual-relay` bootstrap masks 68 logic lines as 16 by packing functions into `;`-chained single-line monstrosities (e.g. `_find_nix`, `_offer_nix_install`, `_ensure_devshell` are each one giant concatenated line). shfmt undoes this — the script becomes honestly 68 lines, which fits under a 100-line carve-out.

### 2. What needs to change (file-by-file)

#### A. `flake.nix` — add `shfmt` package
Line 47: the `packages` list in `pkgs.mkShell` has no `shfmt` entry. Add it alongside the existing tools. shfmt is available in nixpkgs as `shfmt`.

#### B. `ShellSizeGuard.cs` — constants and per-file limit logic
- **Line 10**: `DefaultLimit = 20` → `24`.
- **New constants**: `BootstrapLimit = 100` and `BootstrapPath = "visual-relay"`.
- **`FindViolations`** (line 36–57): Currently applies a single uniform `limit` to every file. Must change to: if `path` equals `BootstrapPath` (ordinal compare), use `BootstrapLimit`; otherwise use the passed `limit`. The `Violation.Limit` must report whichever ceiling actually applied. The env-var/`--max` override still only affects the general limit — the bootstrap ceiling is a fixed constant.
- **`ResolveLimit`** stays as-is (it only resolves the general limit).

#### C. `ShellSizeGuardRunner.cs` — remediation text + enumeration refactor
- **Line 50**: The remediation line `"→ move the logic into a C# tool and leave a thin wrapper; there is no allowlist."` becomes something like `"→ the bootstrap (visual-relay) is the single structural carve-out; all other logic moves to C#."`.
- **Lines 18–44**: The entire `git ls-files` → read files enumeration loop is duplicate #1 of 3. Must be replaced by a call to the new shared `TrackedShellScripts` helper.

#### D. `GuardRunner.ShellSizeAsync` (GuardRunner.cs, lines 48–70) — duplicate enumeration + format check
- **Lines 50–64**: The `git ls-files` → read files enumeration loop is duplicate #2 of 3. Replace with `TrackedShellScripts`.
- After the size check, **add** a `ShellFormatGuard` check: run `shfmt --diff -- <files>` on the same tracked shell scripts. Print diff on exit 1; print the "run ./visual-relay format" hint. On missing binary, print "shfmt not found; run through ./visual-relay so the nix devshell provides it" and fail.
- The method reports both size AND format violations before returning a non-zero exit code — it must not short-circuit after size violations.

#### E. New file: `TrackedShellScripts.cs` in VisualRelay.Guards
A shared helper that:
1. Runs `git ls-files` through `IGitInvoker`
2. Reads each file's first line
3. Filters through `ShellScriptClassifier.IsShellScript`
4. Skips missing/unreadable files
5. Returns `IReadOnlyList<(string Path, string[] Lines)>`

Three call sites must consume it:
- `ShellSizeGuardRunner.RunAsync` (standalone runner)
- `GuardRunner.ShellSizeAsync` (CLI gate)
- `ShellScriptSizeGuardTests.ReadTrackedFilesAsync` (guard-as-test)

The test's `ReadTrackedFilesAsync` retains its own `Assert` calls on `git ls-files` success (they're test-appropriate), but delegates to the shared helper for the enumeration itself.

#### F. New file: `ShellFormatGuard.cs` in VisualRelay.Guards
A guard that:
- Receives a list of `(string Path, string[] Lines)` (the full file data, same shape as the size guard gets — though really it only needs the paths)
- Runs `shfmt --diff -- <paths>` via `ProcessCapture.RunAsync`
- Exit 0 → clean
- Exit 1 → captures output (the diff), returns violations with the diff text and remediation hint
- Missing binary → returns a special violation saying "shfmt not found; run through ./visual-relay so the nix devshell provides it"
- No style flags, no dialect flags — bare invocation (shfmt reads `.editorconfig` natively)

**Problem**: `ProcessCapture` is `internal static partial class` in `VisualRelay.Core`. The Guards project already references VisualRelay.Core, but `ProcessCapture` is internal. Currently `InternalsVisibleTo` in `VisualRelay.Core.csproj` (line 34–38) only grants access to `VisualRelay.Tests` and `VisualRelay.App`. Must add `VisualRelay.Guards`.

#### G. `VisualRelay.Core.csproj` — InternalsVisibleTo
Add `<InternalsVisibleTo Include="VisualRelay.Guards" />` so `ShellFormatGuard` can call `ProcessCapture.RunAsync`.

#### H. `FormatCommand.cs` — add shfmt --write
After `dotnet format` succeeds, run `shfmt --write -- <files>` over the tracked shell scripts (using the same `TrackedShellScripts` enumeration). The command should be async since it uses `ProcessCapture.RunAsync`. Currently `FormatCommand.Run` is synchronous — it'll need to become async or use `Task.Run(...).GetAwaiter().GetResult()` (but given the sync-over-async guard exists, async is the right call; `Program.cs` line 30 already uses `FormatCommand.Run(paths, rest)` — this will need to become `await FormatCommand.RunAsync(paths, rest)`).

Wait — actually `ProcessCapture.RunAsync` is async. Let me check what `FormatCommand` currently does: it calls `ProcessLauncher.Run` which is synchronous. For shfmt we need async. We could either:
- Use `ProcessLauncher.Run("shfmt", ...)` — synchronous, simple, but won't capture output
- Use `ProcessCapture.RunAsync` — async, captures output

Since the format guard needs to run shfmt and capture diff output, we need ProcessCapture. The format command for applying formatting can use ProcessLauncher.Run (sync, no output capture needed) or ProcessCapture. The task says "the command goes async" so ProcessCapture is the right choice.

But wait — `FormatCommand.Run` is called from `Program.cs` line 30 synchronously. If we make it async, Program.cs needs `await`. Looking at Program.cs line 30: `"format" => FormatCommand.Run(paths, rest),` — this is in a switch expression that already mixes sync and async (`"build" => await BuildCommand.RunAsync(...)`). So making format async is fine.

#### I. `CheckCommand.cs` — doc comment update
Line 3–11 doc comment mentions shell-size guard but not shell-format guard. Update to reflect that `check` now also verifies shfmt formatting.

#### J. `Program.cs` (Guards) — dispatch comment
Line 8 mentions only 4 subcommands. Update to reflect the expanded `shell-size` subcommand (which now also runs the format check). The actual dispatch code (line 23) doesn't need to change — `shell-size` still delegates to `ShellSizeGuardRunner.RunAsync`.

#### K. `visual-relay` bootstrap header comment
Line 11: `"Keep this file ≤20 logic lines"` → `"Keep this file ≤100 logic lines (bootstrap carve-out)"`. This is the one hand-edit to script code (comment-only, permitted).

#### L. `ShellScriptSizeGuardTests.cs` — constants, doc comment, synthetic coverage
- **Line 14**: Doc comment `"there is no allowlist"` / `"never excused"` → rewrite to state the bootstrap carve-out and that formatting is enforced by `check`, not this test.
- **Line 50**: `DefaultLimit_IsThe20LineCeiling` asserts 20 → assert 24, rename to `DefaultLimit_IsThe24LineCeiling`. Add a companion test `BootstrapLimit_Is100` pinning `ShellSizeGuard.BootstrapLimit` at 100.
- **Lines 64–70**: `OverLimitScript_IsAViolation_AtLimitScript_IsNot` — the at-limit sample uses 20. Move to 24 (the `atLimit` uses 24, the `over` stays at 25).
- **Line 31**: `ReadTrackedFilesAsync` — replace duplicate enumeration with `TrackedShellScripts` helper (keeping the Assert calls on git success).
- Add new tests: synthetic `visual-relay` at 100 logic lines passes, at 101 violates with `Limit: 100`, and a nested `sub/visual-relay` still gets the general 24.

#### M. `ShellSizeGuardTests.cs` — unit tests for bootstrap carve-out
Add:
- `BootstrapPath_At100_Passes` — synthetic `("visual-relay", CreateScriptLines(100))` with limit=24 → no violations
- `BootstrapPath_At101_Violates` — synthetic `("visual-relay", CreateScriptLines(101))` with limit=24 → one violation with `Limit: 100`
- `NestedBootstrapPath_GetsGeneralLimit` — synthetic `("sub/visual-relay", CreateScriptLines(25))` with limit=24 → one violation with `Limit: 24`

#### N. `WindowsLauncherSizeGuardTests.cs` — stale comment
Line 43: `"well over the 20-line POSIX limit"` → `"well over the 24-line POSIX limit"`.

#### O. `AGENTS.md` — shell formatting section
Add to the "Build & checks" section:
- Shell scripts are shfmt-formatted (apply with `./visual-relay format`, verified by `check`)
- Scripts stay ≤ 24 logic lines with the bootstrap's 100-line carve-out

### 3. Enumeration duplication — the three copies

1. **`ShellSizeGuardRunner.RunAsync`** (line 18–44 in ShellSizeGuardRunner.cs): `git.RunAsync(["ls-files"])` → split output → iterate, check File.Exists, read lines, collect in list.
2. **`GuardRunner.ShellSizeAsync`** (line 50–64 in GuardRunner.cs): Same pattern — `git.RunAsync(["ls-files"])` → split → check File.Exists → read lines.
3. **`ShellScriptSizeGuardTests.ReadTrackedFilesAsync`** (line 78–95 in ShellScriptSizeGuardTests.cs): Same pattern + xUnit `Assert` calls on git success.

The shared `TrackedShellScripts` helper will take an `IGitInvoker` and `repoRoot` and return the list. The test can call it then do its own Assert checks on the git invocation result separately (or the helper can accept a callback/use a pattern where the caller handles git invocation and passes the output). Actually, the cleanest design: the helper takes the raw git-ls-files output string and repo root, does the filtering/reading, and returns the list. Each caller runs git differently (the runners use GitInvoker directly, the test uses it with Assert guards), but they all parse the output the same way.

Actually even better: the helper can take `IGitInvoker` and `repoRoot`, run `git ls-files` internally, and return the file data. For the test, we'd need the helper to not hide the git failure — maybe the helper returns `(int ExitCode, string Output, bool TimedOut, List<...> Files)` and the test can Assert on exitCode before using Files. Or we can have two methods: one that runs git and one that filters.

The simplest approach: `TrackedShellScripts.Enumerate(IGitInvoker git, string repoRoot)` runs git ls-files, splits, reads, filters, and returns `(int ExitCode, List<...> Files)`. The test can Assert on ExitCode.

### 4. ProcessCapture access for Guards

`ProcessCapture` is `internal static partial class` in `VisualRelay.Core.Execution`. The Guards project references Core but can't see internal types. Must add `<InternalsVisibleTo Include="VisualRelay.Guards" />` to `VisualRelay.Core.csproj`.

### 5. No .editorconfig shell section needed

The `.editorconfig` has a `[*.{md,sh,nix}]` section (line 91–93) with only `end_of_line = lf` and `insert_final_newline = true` — no indent settings for shell. shfmt's EditorConfig support will find no matching section for shell and fall back to its defaults (tabs). This is intentional — the task says "No style flags and no `.editorconfig` shell section."

### 6. CI/release.yml

The task says `release.yml` only publishes, never runs check or tests, so no shfmt needed in CI. This is already the case — no changes needed there.
